Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo earlier — helpful to see Redwood's batching and fallback behavior. A couple clarifying points from our side so we can decide between Hosted vs Dedicated vs a VPC/private deploy: 

- Target traffic: average ~25 TPS sustained (chat-style completions), with daily peaks hitting ~180 TPS for short windows (5–15 minutes).
- Token profile: typical request ~120 input tokens + 250 generated tokens (we attach a small sample token distribution). About 60% of requests are short (<=150 total tokens), 40% are long tails.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile ~450ms for short-turn interactions; long-turns can be relaxed to ~1.2s.
- Data posture: PII in prompts occasionally; procurement will want VPC/KMS options if we go beyond hosted.

From the product team: we'd prefer Dedicated if the per-token economics and latency are demonstrably better, but need GPU flavor guidance (H100 vs A100 vs inference-optimized L4) and a clear concurrency model (how many concurrent requests per GPU and how batching will affect latency).

Can you send a concise recommendation table (GPU / expected TPS per node / recommended concurrency / expected 95p latency) and any immediate blockers from a security/compliance perspective? Procurement copied here (procure@edgescale.com) for transparency.

Thanks — Mira

Hi Mira,

Really appreciate the clear traffic profile — that makes sizing straightforward. Recap and recommendation below, plus next steps.

Recap of what you shared:
- Sustained avg: ~25 TPS; peak short bursts ~180 TPS
- Token mix: ~60% short (<150 tokens) / 40% long (up to ~370 tokens)
- Latency SLO: 95p ~450ms for short, ~1.2s for long
- Data: occasional PII; procurement wants VPC/KMS options if we exceed hosted Tier

Short recommendation (dedicated-focused):
- Primary: Dedicated pool with H100 80GB for the initial POC to guarantee latency SLOs and headroom for bursts. H100s give best multi-query throughput for your long-tail generation and faster KV/cache handling.
- Cost-lean option (post-PoC): mix in L4s for short-turn requests (routing by request profile) to reduce unit cost; keep a small H100 reserve for long-turns & fallbacks.

Sizing / expected throughput per node (rough):
- H100 80GB (fp16/flash attention): ~40–60 short-TPS per GPU at <400ms 95p depending on batching window; long-turn throughput ~15–25 TPS. Concurrency: plan 8–12 concurrent active requests per GPU for mixed traffic with a 50ms batching window.
- A100 40GB: ~30–45 short-TPS; long-turn 10–18 TPS. Concurrency similar but slightly tighter memory constraints for long tokens.
- L4 (int8): ~55–80 short-TPS (very cost efficient) but long-turns degrade; recommended for pure short-turn routing only.

Operational notes:
- Prefix/KV cache will help your short-turn latency for repeated prompts — we can enable selective prefix caching for 30–60s windows.
- Batching window tuning: 30–70ms trades off a few ms for cost efficiency; we'll set defaults but tune during PoC.
- Autoscale: configure a minimal baseline (1–2 H100) plus burst capacity policy to bring additional H100s online for sustained >120 TPS.

Security/compliance blockers:
- Hosted: acceptable for initial PoC with our SOC2/ISO attestations, but procurement's VPC/KMS ask pushes you toward Dedicated/Private for production.
- Private/VPC: supported; we'll need network egress rules and an approved KMS integration (we support AWS KMS & GCP KMS).

Attachments: I attached a short sizing matrix and a draft SLA for procurement to review.

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal sizing review with our SEs (can you confirm availability for a 45-minute session this week?)
2) Share token sample (you already attached; we'll validate the token distribution against our bench)
3) PoC plan: 2-week reserved pool (1 H100 + 2 L4s) to collect telemetry and tune batching/caching

If that aligns, I'll loop in Neha and Priyom for the deep sizing + PoC scoping.

Thanks — Vivek

--

Quick sizing response (high level) — deliverable for PoC plan below.

1) Short answer on GPUs: H100 recommended as primary for PoC to meet the 95p latency target for mixed token workloads. A100 is viable if H100 isn't available but requires slightly larger cluster. L4s should be used as supplementary nodes for short-turn routing to reduce cost.

2) PoC footprint (2-week run) suggestion:
- Baseline pool: 2 x H100 80GB (handles steady 25 TPS + short bursts up to ~90 TPS without autoscale)
- Burst policy: autoscale add 2 additional H100s when sustained >120 TPS for 2+ minutes
- Cost-optimization set: 3 x L4 nodes to route short-turn traffic (we can start with 1 and ramp to 3 based on telemetry)
- Routing rules: client-side header to mark short vs long (we provide a small SDK flag) + server-side traffic classifier for fallback.

3) Concurrency & batching config:
- Concurrency target: 10 active requests per H100 for mixed traffic (reserve concurrency headroom for KV-heavy requests).
- Batching window: start at 50ms for PoC; if 95p latency is tight, reduce to 30ms during A/B tuning.
- KV cache TTL: 45s for conversational threads; enable prefix caching for repeated prompts.

4) Expected 95p latency (estimates from bench, subject to PoC validation):
- H100 baseline (with 50ms batching + KV): short-turn 95p ~320–420ms; long-turn 95p ~700–900ms.
- With L4 routing for short-turns: short-turn 95p ~240–360ms for routed requests.

5) PoC checklist / next actions:
- EdgeScale: confirm two-week window and provide any additional token samples (we have edgescale-token-profile.csv).
- Redwood: provision baseline 2x H100 + 1 L4 immediately for PoC start; enable telemetry snapshot exports to shared S3.
- Security: procurement to send required network egress rules and KMS contact; our infra team will produce a short VPC connectivity checklist.

I'll draft a short runbook for the PoC (1–2 pages) and a simple cost estimate for the proposed footprint. Vivek — okay to send this to Mira and Procurement as a proposed plan?

Cheers — Neha
